_comment: Scenarios executed by run-all-benchmarks.sh. Each entry: script (a bench-*.sh),
category, label, and a params object whose keys are that script's flag names in
The first six mirror nats/scripts/scenarios.json and fast-dds/scripts/scenarios.json
one-for-one (baseline / large-message / multi-client throughput, RTT check, steady
one-way latency, scalability sweep) so the three projects' run-index.csv files can be
The trailing entries cover what is specific to Aeron. Two of them exist to keep the
comparison honest in opposite directions: 'ipc-1000' is Aeron doing something NATS Core
cannot (shared memory, ~2us), and 'stock-driver-defaults' is Aeron measured WITHOUT the
low-latency media driver settings this project turns on by default. Leaving the first
out would flatter NATS by omission; leaving the second out would flatter Aeron, because
every other row here is measured with a busy-spinning driver that an out-of-the-box
deployment does not have. Measured gap: p50 21-41us (noop) vs 245-331us (backoff), i.e. 8-14x.

scenarios.label: default-sweep
scenarios._comment: poll-idle yield, not the default busy: 25 busy-spinning subscriber threads plus the driver's 3 exceed the core count on any ordinary machine, and oversubscribing there does not just slow the result down - the clients can time out against the driver and abort. msgs-per-sub is 20000 rather than fast-dds/'s 5000 because Aeron is fast enough that 5000 messages complete in ~10ms, which is startup noise rather than a steady state.

scenarios.label: ipc-1000
scenarios._comment: aeron:ipc - shared memory through the driver's term buffers, bypassing the sender/receiver threads and the kernel UDP stack entirely. No NATS Core counterpart; the Fast DDS counterpart is --transport shm.

scenarios.label: stock-driver-defaults
scenarios._comment: The same run as steady-1000 but with Aeron's OWN defaults for the media driver's idle strategy and a sleeping poll loop. This is what an unconfigured deployment gets, and it is the honest counterweight to every other row in this file.

scenarios.label: slow-subscriber
scenarios._comment: sub-work-us simulates application processing per message. Under Fast DDS BEST_EFFORT this would show up as msg_loss; under Aeron it shows up as back-pressure on the publisher and a lower achieved rate, with loss still zero. That difference is the point of the scenario. term-length 64k is REQUIRED, not tuning: at Aeron's default term length the whole 50000x128B run fits inside the publication window, so offer() never waits and the run reports pub 1.61M/s against sub 48k/s with ZERO back-pressure - measuring how fast a buffer fills, not throughput. With 64k it produces 1.49M back-pressure events and a publisher rate that converges on the subscriber's.
